s1.syndrome_frame: Pelvic mass with chronic abdominal pain and vaginal discharge
salient_findings: Pelvic mass extending to two fingers below the umbilicus
key_facts: 48-year-old postmenopausal woman
Gravida 2, para 2
3-month history of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge
Fluctuating lower abdominal pain
Fever
Progressive abdominal enlargement over 15 years
Difficulty with defecation and voiding
Previous attempted myomectomy with severe adhesions
Elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level of 115.6 g/dL
Smooth, firm pelvic mass on rectovaginal examination
Limited mobility of the pelvic mass
Cervix could not be visualized or sondaged
Transabdominal ultrasound showed a hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity
Separate homogeneous solid mass in the left adnexa
Abdominal and pelvic computed tomography demonstrated a multilocular cystic mass

shortlist.label: Uterine fibroid with cystic degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Pelvic mass with cystic degeneration and elevated CA-125 level

shortlist.label: Infected hematometra
shortlist.why_kept: Brown-yellowish vaginal discharge, fever, and pelvic mass with fluid and air on imaging

shortlist.label: Endometrioid adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CA-125 level and pelvic mass with solid components on imaging

shortlist.label: Uterine leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid growth of pelvic mass and elevated CA-125 level

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Multilocular cystic mass on imaging with potential for malignant transformation

raw.rationale: The patient's history of progressive abdominal enlargement, difficulty with defecation and voiding, and previous attempted myomectomy with severe adhesions, combined with imaging findings of a hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity and a separate solid mass in the left adnexa, are more consistent with a large uterine fibroid causing obstruction and infection, rather than a malignant process like leiomyosarcoma.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: While the elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level and the presence of a large pelvic mass could suggest a malignant process, the patient's long history of symptoms and the presence of a separate solid mass in the left adnexa, which could represent a fibroid, make leiomyosarcoma less likely.
